about: Sonic Advance 2's parts, in the order a player meets them, then its other characters and modes. Each counts the same. A part is proven when a recording plays it from its first frame to its last and every frame matches the original: "frames" are the first and last of the recording's frames it covers. A part may end with a press that moves the game on, the way a player leaves it, such as Start on the title screen. Where the screen is one colour between two parts, those frames go with the part before. Foundations are what many parts need but no player would call a part, and they don't count towards the parts.

foundations.name: An act's opening
foundations.what: Leaf Forest act 1 from its first frame until a player can move, with nothing pressed once its title card is left: its layers, the camera, the numbers, Sonic, the machine and the countdown, and the song and the announcer. A recording can start here from a start point, so nothing before it in the game has to be ready first.

foundations.name: A character running
foundations.what: Sonic setting off as the countdown ends, START!!, then running, turning and braking both ways on Leaf Forest's ground and slopes, with the camera following.

foundations.name: A character jumping
foundations.what: Sonic jumping, falling and landing, rolling, and meeting walls and ceilings.

foundations.name: Rings
foundations.what: Sonic running through Leaf Forest act 1's rings: taking them, their sound and the number going up.

foundations.name: Springs
foundations.what: Sonic thrown by Leaf Forest act 1's springs, with the camera following, falling back to the ground.

foundations.name: Being hit
foundations.what: Leaf Forest act 1's first enemies moving and hitting Sonic, his rings scattering and his blinking after it, and beating one with a jump.

foundations.name: The platforming
foundations.what: A character running and jumping through a whole stretch of an act, with every piece it needs together. Everything played in a zone builds on it.
